titulo: Listen before you speak: First dialogue

aula.objetivo: Recognise the first 12 Cyrillic sounds, read the first words, hear the stress and say the first sentences.

blocos.contexto: Two people look at a family photo.

linhas.pt: — And this one, who is she?
— This is the sister. Here is the juice.

blocos.titulo: Unstressed vowels: «о» sounds like «а» and «е» sounds like «и»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: A stressed vowel is clear and long. An unstressed vowel is weak and short, and it changes its sound. This is called vowel reduction. STEP 2: Unstressed «о» sounds like «а». In «она» (ah-NAH), the first letter is «о», but you say «ah». In «Москва» (mahsk-VAH), you say «mah», not «moh». STEP 3: Stressed «о» stays «о». In «кот» (koht) and in «метро» (mee-TROH), the «о» carries the stress and sounds like «о». STEP 4: Unstressed «е» sounds almost like «и», a quick «ee». In «метро», the first syllable sounds like «mee». In «сестра» (sees-TRAH), it sounds like «sees». In «ресторан» (rees-tah-RAHN), it sounds like «rees». STEP 5: The respelling next to each word, in this course, already shows the real pronunciation. When it differs from the spelling, trust the respelling and the audio.
blocos.comparacao: you already do this in English without noticing: the unstressed «a» in «banana» or «about» turns into a weak «uh». In Russian the same happens to the «о» and the «е» that are far from the stress.

exemplos.pt: metro: the «е» sounds like «и», read mee-TROH

tabela.what_happens: «е» sounds like «и» and the middle «о» sounds like «а»

erros.motivo: Unstressed, the «е» sounds like «и» and the stress falls on «ро»: mee-TROH.

blocos.titulo: Voiced and voiceless consonants: the end of the word changes
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: A voiced consonant is one where your throat vibrates. Put a hand on your throat and say «v»: you feel it vibrate. Now say «f»: it does not vibrate. «f» is the voiceless partner of «v». STEP 2: Russian has pairs like this: «в» and «ф», «б» and «п», «д» and «т», «г» and «к», «з» and «с», «ж» and «ш». The first of each pair is the voiced one. Today you already know the voiced «в» and the voiceless «к», «т» and «с». The others come in the next lesson. STEP 3: The end-of-word rule: at the end of a word, a voiced consonant loses its vibration and becomes its voiceless partner. That is why «Романов» (rah-MAH-nahf) ends with an «f» sound, although it is written with «в». STEP 4: The neighbour rule: a voiced consonant also becomes voiceless before a voiceless one. In «вкус» (fkoos), which means «taste», the «в» sounds like «f» because it comes before «к». STEP 5: The spelling does not change, only the sound. Always write the word the way it is spelled, and speak the way the audio speaks.
blocos.comparacao: in English the difference between «v» and «f» changes the word: «van» and «fan». It does in Russian too. But at the end of a word that difference disappears and only the voiceless sound is pronounced.

exemplos.pt: surname: read rah-MAH-nahf, with an «f» at the end

tabela.why: «в» at the end of a word sounds like «ф»
«в» at the end of a word sounds like «ф»

erros.motivo: The final «в» loses its vibration: rah-MAH-nahf.

itens.explicacao: The sentence starts with «Кто» (who). «Как дела?» starts with «как» and «Это мама» is not a question.
The last word is «сестра» (sees-TRAH), with the «с» at the start and the «р» in the middle.
The last word has one syllable and ends in k: «сок».
It is read ah-NAH, with the stress on «NAH». That is why the «о» of the first syllable, unstressed, sounds like «а».
The unstressed «е» sounds almost like «и» and the stress falls on «ро»: mee-TROH.
The unstressed «о» sounds like «а» and the stress falls on «ква»: mahsk-VAH.

itens.enunciado: How does the «в» sound at the end of «Романов»?
itens.explicacao: At the end of a word, the voiced «в» loses its vibration and becomes the voiceless «ф»: rah-MAH-nahf.
The question «Кто это?» asks for a person. «сестра» is a person; «как» and «нет» do not answer «who».
«Как дела?» is the fixed question for «how are you?». With «Кто» the sentence would mean «who goes».
To introduce someone, you say «Это» and the name, with no verb in the middle.
Four letters in «Это» and then the name. The name is read as it is written, with the stressed «о»: ahn-TOHN.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Here is the restaurant.»
itens.explicacao: To point something out, you say «Вот» first and then the thing. Russian has no «is» here.

blocos.enunciado: Point to a photo (or imagine one) and ask «Кто это?». Answer with «Это мама.», «Это сестра.» and «Это Антон.». Also say «Романов» the way it is pronounced: rah-MAH-nahf.
blocos.exemplo: Кто это? Это мама. Это сестра. Это Антон.

blocos.enunciado: Listen and choose: «сок», «сор» or «вот». Identify which word you heard.
